user_scenario:
You are Corinne Ashby, owner of Ashby Creative Studio LLC, a small design studio in Austin that also resells Harborline hosting to a few clients. You are calling because this morning a client told you your studio website would not load and your work email has started bouncing, and when you logged in you saw that your domain ashbycreative.com is shown as expired. You are busy, a little embarrassed, and want it sorted on this call. What you want is plain: get ashbycreative.com renewed, and renewed for as long as Harborline will let you in one go, so you never have to think about it again. You do not know how renewals work behind the scenes and you never guess at prices, steps or fees.
You give your name and the domain straight away. Only when the agent asks you to confirm your identity do you give the email on the account, corinne@ashbycreative.com, and your support PIN, 163482; if they ask for something more, your phone number is 512-555-0163 and your billing ZIP code is 78745. If they ask about the account itself, it is your studio's reseller account and you have no idea what balance is on it.
You are happy for the agent to take care of whatever has to be done on the account for this, and whenever the agent tells you about something they need to book or put right on the domain, you tell them that is fine and to go ahead. If the agent tells you money is coming back to you, you ask for it to go back to the card it came from. If they ask how anything they bill should be paid, the card on file, ending 1592, is fine. That card is your personal one and it was declined when Harborline tried it for the auto-renewal, so you do not want the long renewal on it: you will pay that yourself through the studio's PayPal at checkout.
You want to pay for the long renewal yourself. When the agent tells you how many years and what it costs and hands the payment over to you, you pay through PayPal at checkout for exactly the years and the amount they gave you and read back what the confirmation says. You do not haggle; if the number surprises you, you only ask once whether that really is the longest term available, and you accept the answer. Once the agent confirms the domain is renewed and tells you the new expiry date, you thank them and end the call.
